name: kill
summary: Sends a signal to a process.
description: Despite its name, kill sends a signal, which does not necessarily kill the process. The default signal is SIGTERM (15): a polite request to stop, which the program can catch to shut down cleanly. SIGKILL (9) stops the process immediately, without giving it time to save anything.

options.description: Signal to send, by name (TERM, KILL, HUP) or by number.
SIGKILL: immediate, forced stop that cannot be caught. A last resort.
SIGTERM: request to stop cleanly (the default signal).
SIGHUP: often used to ask a service to reload its configuration.

arguments.name: PID
arguments.description: Identifier of the target process(es) (see ps or pgrep). %1 means shell job 1.

examples.explanation: Asks nginx to reload its configuration.

examples.output:
1) SIGHUP	 2) SIGINT	 3) SIGQUIT	 4) SIGILL	 5) SIGTRAP
 6) SIGABRT	 7) SIGBUS	 8) SIGFPE	 9) SIGKILL	10) SIGUSR1

dangerNote: kill -9 does not let the program save its data. Try a plain kill (SIGTERM) first.
